/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/branca.desc: A refreshing mixture of bitter Fernet with mint creme liquour.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/branca.name: Branca Menta

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/brandy.desc: The far more gussied-up ancestor of the Sidecar, this heavily garnished cocktail is the grandparent of many essential drinks served today.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/brandy.name: Brandy Crusta

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/brave_.desc: It's just as effective as Dutch-Courage!
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/brave_.name: Brave Bull

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/bug_sp.desc: A harsh, acrid, bitter drink, for those who need something to brace themselves.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/bug_sp.name: Bug Spray

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/casino.desc: A gin-heavy classic. Juniper is tempered by scant amounts of citrus and sweetened with liqueur.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/casino.name: Casino

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/champa.desc: A sparkling wine known for its ability to strike fast and hard.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/champa.name: Champagne

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/change.desc: You take a tiny sip and feel a burning sensation...
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/change.name: Changeling Sting

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/coconu.desc: The distilled essence of the beach. Tastes like bleach-blonde hair and suncream.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/coconu.name: Coconut Rum

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/cognac.desc: A sweet and strongly alcoholic drink, made after numerous distillations and years of maturing. Classy as fornication.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/cognac.name: Cognac

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/creme_.desc: A chocolatey liqueur excellent for adding dessert notes to beverages and bribing sororities.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/creme_.name: Creme de Cacao

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/creme_.desc: A coconut liqueur for smooth, creamy, tropical drinks.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/creme_.name: Creme de Coconut

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/creme_.desc: A minty liqueur excellent for refreshing, cool drinks.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/creme_.name: Creme de Menthe

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/cuba_l.desc: Viva la Revolucion! Viva Cuba Libre!
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/cuba_l.name: Cuba Libre

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/curaca.desc: Made with laraha oranges, for an aromatic finish.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/curaca.name: Curaçao

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/daiqui.desc: In some ways the ultimate tropical cocktail, very few rum drinks are not in some way a descendant of this classic.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/daiqui.name: Daiquiri

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/dark_a.desc: A classic drink arriving to thunderous applause.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/dark_a.name: Dark and Stormy

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/driest.desc: Only for the experienced. You think you see sand floating in the glass.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/driest.name: Driest Martini

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/drunke.desc: Look, if you had to get into a shootout in the cold vacuum of space, you'd want to be drunk too.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/drunke.name: Drunken Espatier

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/drunke.desc: A weird mix of whiskey and blumpkin juice.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/drunke.name: Drunken Blumpkin

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/duplex.desc: An inseparable combination of two fruity drinks.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/duplex.name: Duplex

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/eggnog.desc: For enjoying the most wonderful time of the year.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/eggnog.name: Eggnog

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ersatz.desc: Sweet, bitter, spicy- that's a great combination.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ersatz.name: Ersatzche

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fanciu.desc: What if the Manhattan cocktail ACTUALLY used a bitter herb liquour? Helps you sober up.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fanciu.name: Fanciulli

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fernet.desc: An incredibly bitter herbal liqueur used as a digestif.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fernet.name: Fernet

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fernet.desc: A very popular and bittersweet digestif, ideal after a heavy meal. Best served on a sawed-off cola bottle as per tradition.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fernet.name: Fernet Cola

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fetchi.desc: Whiskey sour/iron/uranium mixture resulting in a highly magnetic slurry. Mild alcohol content.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fetchi.name: Fetching Fizz

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/flip_c.desc: A simplified and modernized adaptation of a much older drink that predates the Cocktail. While the older version used ale and was heated before it was drunk, this version is chilled. Really, the main similarity is the use of a whole egg.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/flip_c.name: Flip Cocktail

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/four_b.desc: A drink to power your typing hands.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/four_b.name: Four Bit

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/french.desc: A sophisticated cocktail made by strengthening champagne with gin, then flavoring with lemon juice and sugar.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/french.name: French 75

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fringe.desc: Bubbly, classy, and undoubtedly strong - a Glitch City classic.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fringe.name: Fringe Weaver

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fruit_.desc: A wine made from grown plants.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/fruit_.name: Fruit Wine

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/gariba.desc: Named for the 19th-century Italian general, the red-orange color scheme of this drink mimics the shirts of those who followed him into battles all across the world.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/gariba.name: Garibaldi

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/gin.desc: It's gin. In space. I say, good sir.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/gin.name: Gin

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/gin_ga.desc: Excellent cooling alcoholic drink with not so ordinary taste.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/gin_ga.name: Gin Garden

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ginger.desc: A delightfully simple cocktail that pleases the senses.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ginger.name: Ginger Amaretto

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ginton.desc: An all time classic, mild cocktail.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ginton.name: Gin and Tonic

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/godfat.desc: A rough cocktail with illegal connections.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/godfat.name: Godfather

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/godmot.desc: A twist on a classic, liked more by mature women.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/godmot.name: Godmother

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/goldsc.desc: 100 proof cinnamon schnapps, made for alcoholic teen girls on spring break.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/goldsc.name: Goldschlager

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/grappa.desc: A fine Italian brandy, for when regular wine just isn't alcoholic enough for you.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/grappa.name: Grappa

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/grassh.desc: A fresh and sweet dessert shooter. Difficult to look manly while drinking this.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/grassh.name: Grasshopper

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hearty.desc: Brave bull/syndicate bomb/absinthe mixture resulting in an energizing beverage. Mild alcohol content.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hearty.name: Hearty Punch

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/helian.desc: A dark yet radiant mixture of absinthe and hallucinogens. The choice of all true artists.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/helian.name: Helianthus

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/herbal.desc: A liqueur made with a wide variety of herbs and spices, infused into spirit through both distillation and maceration. So many, in fact, that trying to pick them out by scent and taste seems nearly impossible...
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/herbal.name: Herbal Liqueur

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hippie.desc: You just don't get it maaaan.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hippie.name: Hippie's Delight

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/honeyb.desc: Mead sweetened and flavoured with lemon.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/honeyb.name: Honeybee Mead

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hooch.desc: Either someone's failure at cocktail making or attempt in alcohol production. In any case, do you really want to drink that?
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hooch.name: Hooch

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hot_to.desc: A warmed blend of spirits, sugar, and spices. While the concept is ancient, this preparation with cognac and refined sugar is a bit more modern.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/hot_to.name: Hot Toddy

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/iced_b.desc: A beer which is so cold the air around it freezes.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/iced_b.name: Iced Beer

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/imperi.desc: For when orgeat is in short supply, do as the spacers do- make do and mend.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/imperi.name: Imperial Mai Tai

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/improv.desc: The Classic Whiskey cocktail improved by the addition of absinthe and maraschino, as well as swapping the typical orange peel garnish for lemon.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/improv.name: Improved Whiskey Cocktail

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/irish_.desc: Whiskey-imbued cream, what else would you expect from the Irish?
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/irish_.name: Irish Cream

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/irishc.desc: Mmm, tastes like the free Irish state.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/irishc.name: Irish Car Bomb

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/irishc.desc: Coffee, and alcohol. More fun than a Mimosa to drink in the morning.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/irishc.name: Irish Coffee

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/jack_r.desc: A light cocktail perfect for sipping with a slice of pie.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/jack_r.name: Jack Rose

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/jungle.desc: This late-tiki concoction leverages the brilliant combination of bitter liqueur and pineapple juice to make a remarkably well-balanced cocktail.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/jungle.name: Jungle Bird

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kahlua.desc: A widely known, Mexican coffee-flavoured liqueur. In production since 1936!
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kahlua.name: Kahlua

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kings_.desc: A stiff, bitter drink with an odd name and odder recipe.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kings_.name: King's Ransom

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/konoco.desc: Coconut rum, coffee liqueur, and espresso- an odd combination, to be sure, but a welcomed one.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/konoco.name: Konococo Rumtini

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kortar.desc: A sweet, milky nut-based drink enjoyed on Tizira. Frequently mixed with fruit juices and cocoa for extra refreshment.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kortar.name: Kortara

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kumich.desc: A new take on a classic cocktail, the Kumicho takes the Godfather formula and adds shochu for an Asian twist.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/kumich.name: Kumichō

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/last_w.desc: Despite being invented at the turn of the 20th century, this drink fell into obscurity until the cocktail renaissance of the beginning of the 21st, where it then went on to dominate bars and inspire countless twists upon its formula.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/last_w.name: Last Word

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/lizard.desc: An alcoholic beverage from Space China, made by infusing lizard tails in ethanol.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/lizard.name: Lizard Wine

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/long_h.desc: A favourite amongst freighter pilots, unscrupulous smugglers, and nerf herders.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/long_h.name: Long Haul

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/long_j.desc: A long drink of navy rum, bitters, and lemonade. Particularly popular aboard the Mothic Fleet as it's light on ration credits and heavy on flavour.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/long_j.name: Long John Silver

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/longis.desc: The liquor cabinet, brought together in a delicious mix. Intended for middle-aged alcoholic women only.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/longis.name: Long Island Iced Tea

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/maltsh.desc: A slightly alcoholic but sweet milkshake
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/maltsh.name: Malt Milkshake

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/manhat.desc: The Detective's undercover drink of choice. He never could stomach gin...
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/manhat.name: Manhattan

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/manhat.desc: A scientist's drink of choice, for pondering ways to blow up the station.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/manhat.name: Manhattan Project

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/manly_.desc: Beer and Ale, brought together in a delicious mix. Intended for true men only.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/manly_.name: The Manly Dorf

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/marasc.desc: A classic sweet liqueur made from the fruits, leaves, and even branches of sour cherries. Surprisingly, it doesn't actually taste much like cherry.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/marasc.name: Maraschino Liqueur

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/margar.desc: On the rocks with salt on the rim. Arriba~!
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/margar.name: Margarita

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/martin.desc: Vermouth with Gin. Not quite how 007 enjoyed it, but still delicious.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/martin.name: Classic Martini

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mary_p.desc: Named after an early 20th-century film star, this cocktail takes a rum and pineapple flavor profile and presents it in a classier and more elegant form than one would typically expect.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mary_p.name: Mary Pickford

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/maui_s.desc: Behind this drink's red facade lurks a sharp, complex flavour.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/maui_s.name: Maui Sunrise

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mauna_.desc: Extremely hot; not for the faint of heart!
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mauna_.name: Mauna Loa

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mead.desc: A Viking drink, though a cheap one.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mead.name: Mead

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mojito.desc: A drink that looks as refreshing as it tastes.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mojito.name: Mojito

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/moonsh.desc: You've really hit rock bottom now... your liver packed its bags and left last night.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/moonsh.name: Moonshine

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/moscow.desc: A chilly drink that reminds you of the Derelict.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/moscow.name: Moscow Mule

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mushi_.desc: A popular summer beverage on Tizira, made from sweetened mushroom tea.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/mushi_.name: Mushi Kombucha

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/narsou.desc: Side effects include self-mutilation and hoarding plasteel.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/narsou.name: Nar'Sour

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/navy_r.desc: Rum as the finest sailors drink.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/navy_r.name: Navy Rum

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/negron.desc: An iconic Italian aperitif, its simple intensity crowns it as perhaps the ultimate bitter cocktail. Supposedly it was named after an Italian count who wanted a stronger version of a spritz and asked his bartender to replace soda with gin.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/negron.name: Negroni

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/nekomi.desc: An overly sweet cocktail, made with melon liqueur, melon juice, and champagne (which contains no melon, unfortunately).
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/nekomi.name: Nekomimosa

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/neurot.desc: A strong neurotoxin that puts the subject into a death-like state.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/neurot.name: Neurotoxin

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/nuclea.desc: Overproof, funky, pot still rum and herbal liqueur takes the simple elegance of a Cuban daiquiri and turns it on its head.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/nuclea.name: Nuclear daiquiri

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/nuclea.desc: A drink for those who enjoy the gnarlier things in life, like high-ester rums and Cobalt 60.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/nuclea.name: Thermonuclear Daiquiri

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/old_fa.desc: By some measures the first cocktail, made by flavoring a hard spirit with sugar and bitters, with the spirit in question most often being whiskey in modern times.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/old_fa.name: Old Fashioned

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/old_ti.desc: An archaic potation enjoyed by old coots of all ages.

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pepper.name: Peppermint Patty

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pina_c.desc: A fresh pineapple drink with coconut rum. Yum.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pina_c.name: Pina Colada

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pina_o.desc: An oddly designed concoction of olive oil and pineapple juice.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pina_o.name: Piña Olivada

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/planet.desc: This jubilant drink celebrates humanity's triumph over the alien menace. May be offensive to non-human crewmembers.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/planet.name: Planet Cracker

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pod_te.desc: Ride the lightning!  Recharges etherials, suppresses phobias, and gives strong temporary shock resistance.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pod_te.name: Pod Tesla

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/poets_.desc: This cocktail takes a classic martini base and twists it into a deliciously sweet and herbal mode. Nanotrasen regulations state not to drink this too soon before sleep, or risk 'oneiric encroachment,' whatever that means.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/poets_.name: Poet's Dream

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pousse.desc: An aesthetically beautiful cocktail made from the careful and meticulous layering of various liquors. Extremely annoying to make.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pousse.name: Pousse Cafe

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/protei.desc: A vile blend of protein, pure grain alcohol, korta flour, and blood. Useful for bulking up, if you can keep it down.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/protei.name: Protein Blend

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pruno.desc: Fermented prison wine made from fruit, sugar, and despair. Security loves to confiscate this, which is the only kind thing Security has ever done.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/pruno.name: Pruno

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/quadru.desc: Kicks just as hard as licking the power cell on a baton, but tastier.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/quadru.name: Quadruple Sec

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/quintu.desc: Law, Order, Alcohol, and Police Brutality distilled into one single elixir of JUSTICE.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/quintu.name: Quintuple Sec

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ramos_.desc: A complex twist on the concept of a gin fizz, adding cream and egg white along side lemon juice for an incomparable textural experience. In this version, the drink's signature usage of orange blossom water is replaced with a drop of orange liqueur.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ramos_.name: Ramos Gin Fizz

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ratvan.desc: Side effects include hoarding brass and hatred of blood.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ratvan.name: Rat'vander Cocktail

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/red_ci.desc: A breakfast drink from New Osaka, for when you really need to get drunk at 9:30 in the morning in more socially acceptable manner than drinking bagwine on the bullet train. Not that you should drink this on the bullet train either.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/red_ci.name: Red City AM

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/red_me.desc: The true Viking drink! Even though it has a strange red color.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/red_me.name: Red Mead

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/red_pl.desc: Made in celebration of the Martian Concession, the Red Planet is based on the classic El Presidente, and is as patriotic as it is bright crimson.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/red_pl.name: Red Planet

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/rice_b.desc: A light, rice-based lagered beer popular on Mars. Considered a hate crime against Bavarians under the Reinheitsgebot Act of 1516.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/rice_b.name: Rice Beer

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ritual.desc: The dangerous, potent, alcoholic component of ritual wine.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/ritual.name: Ritual Wine

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/rubber.desc: A quality rubberneck should not contain any gross natural ingredients.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/rubber.name: Rubberneck

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/saibas.desc: A drink glorifying Cybersun's enduring business.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/saibas.name: Saibāsan

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sake.desc: A sweet rice wine of questionable legality and extreme potency.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sake.name: Sake

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/salt_a.desc: A bracing sour with an interesting salty taste.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/salt_a.name: Salt and Swell

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sangri.desc: A blood-red wine punch strengthened with liquor and sweetened with as much chopped fruit as one can get their hands on.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sangri.name: Sangria

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sanrai.desc: It's a melon cream soda, except with alcohol- what's not to love? Well... possibly the hangovers.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sanrai.name: Sanraizusōda

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sazera.desc: Whiskey made aromatic by absinthe and creole bitters.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sazera.name: Sazerac

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sbiten.desc: A spicy Vodka! Might be a little hot for the little guys!
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sbiten.name: Sbiten

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/screwd.desc: Vodka, mixed with plain ol' orange juice. The result is surprisingly delicious.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/screwd.name: Screwdriver

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sea_br.desc: Light and refreshing with a mint and cocoa hit- like mint choc chip ice cream you can drink!
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sea_br.name: Sea Breeze

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sentai.desc: Based on the galaxy-famous "Kyūkyoku no Ninja Pawā Sentai", the Sentai Quencha is a favourite at anime conventions and weeb bars.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sentai.name: Sentai Quencha

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/shochu.desc: Also known as soju or baijiu, this drink is made from fermented rice, much like sake, but at a generally higher proof making it more similar to a true spirit.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/shochu.name: Shochu

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sideca.desc: The one ride you'll gladly give up the wheel for.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/sideca.name: Sidecar

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/spritz.desc: This bittersweet and refreshing aperitif brings to mind the beautiful summer sunsets of venice.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/spritz.name: Spritz

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/squirt.desc: Fermented squirt extract with a nose of stale bread and ocean water. Whatever a squirt is.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/squirt.name: Squirt Cider

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/star.desc: A blend of applejack and vermouth accented with bitters.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/star.name: Star

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/stinge.desc: A snappy way to end the day.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/stinge.name: Stinger

/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/suffer.desc: A tiki style hangover cure made from ginger beer, spirits, and bitters.
/datum/reagent/consumable/ethanol/suffer.name: Suffering Bastard

If overdosed the subject will move randomly, laugh randomly, drop items and suffer from Toxin and Brain damage. If addicted the subject will constantly jitter and drool, before becoming dizzy and losing motor control and eventually suffer heavy toxin damage.
/datum/reagent/drug/methamphetamine.name: Methamphetamine

/datum/reagent/drug/methamphetamine/robo.desc: An experimental excitement chemical for synthetic life, this produces a similar effect to methamphetamine, but on robots.
/datum/reagent/drug/methamphetamine/robo.name: Positronic Excitement Salts

/datum/reagent/drug/mushroomhallucinogen.desc: A strong hallucinogenic drug derived from certain species of mushroom.
/datum/reagent/drug/mushroomhallucinogen.name: Mushroom Hallucinogen

/datum/reagent/drug/nicotine.desc: Slightly reduces stun times. If overdosed it will deal toxin and oxygen damage.
/datum/reagent/drug/nicotine.name: Nicotine

/datum/reagent/drug/pumpup.desc: Take on the world! A fast acting, hard hitting drug that pushes the limit on what you can handle.
/datum/reagent/drug/pumpup.name: Pump-Up

/datum/reagent/drug/saturnx.desc: This compound was first discovered during the infancy of cloaking technology and at the time thought to be a promising candidate agent. It was withdrawn for consideration after the researchers discovered a slew of associated safety issues including thought disorders and hepatoxicity.
/datum/reagent/drug/saturnx.name: Saturn-X

/datum/reagent/drug/saturnx/stable.desc: A chemical extract originating from the Saturn-X compound, stabilized and safer for tactical use. After the recipe was discovered, it was planned to be put into mass production, but the program fell apart after its lead disappeared and was never seen again.
/datum/reagent/drug/saturnx/stable.name: Stabilized Saturn-X

/datum/reagent/drug/space_drugs.desc: An illegal chemical compound used as drug.
/datum/reagent/drug/space_drugs.name: Space Drugs

/datum/reagent/drying_agent.desc: A desiccant. Can be used to dry things.
/datum/reagent/drying_agent.name: Drying Agent

/datum/reagent/eigenstate.desc: A strange mixture formed from a controlled reaction of bluespace with plasma, that causes localised eigenstate fluxuations within the patient
/datum/reagent/eigenstate.name: Eigenstasium

/datum/reagent/eldritch.desc: A strange liquid that defies the laws of physics.  		It re-energizes and heals those who can see beyond this fragile reality,  but is incredibly harmful to the closed-minded. It metabolizes very quickly.
/datum/reagent/eldritch.name: Eldritch Essence

/datum/reagent/exotic_stabilizer.desc: Advanced compound created by mixing stabilizing agent and hyper-plasmium oxide.
/datum/reagent/exotic_stabilizer.name: Exotic Stabilizer

/datum/reagent/firefighting_foam.desc: A historical fire suppressant. Originally believed to simply displace oxygen to starve fires, it actually interferes with the combustion reaction itself. Vastly superior to the cheap water-based extinguishers found on NT vessels.
/datum/reagent/firefighting_foam.name: Firefighting Foam

/datum/reagent/fluorine.desc: A comically-reactive chemical element. The universe does not want this stuff to exist in this form in the slightest.
/datum/reagent/fluorine.name: Fluorine

/datum/reagent/fluorosurfactant.desc: A perfluoronated sulfonic acid that forms a foam when mixed with water.
/datum/reagent/fluorosurfactant.name: Fluorosurfactant

/datum/reagent/foaming_agent.desc: An agent that yields metallic foam when mixed with light metal and a strong acid.
/datum/reagent/foaming_agent.name: Foaming Agent

/datum/reagent/fuel/oil.desc: Burns in a small smoky fire, can be used to get Ash.
/datum/reagent/fuel/oil.name: Oil

/datum/reagent/fuel/unholywater.desc: Something that shouldn't exist on this plane of existence.
/datum/reagent/fuel/unholywater.name: Unholy Water

/datum/reagent/glitter.desc: if you can see this description, contact a coder.
/datum/reagent/glitter.name: Generic Glitter

/datum/reagent/glitter/confetti.desc: Tiny plastic flakes that are impossible to sweep up.
/datum/reagent/glitter/confetti.name: Confetti

/datum/reagent/gluttonytoxin.desc: An advanced corruptive toxin produced by something terrible.
/datum/reagent/gluttonytoxin.name: Gluttony's Blessing

/datum/reagent/glycerol.desc: Glycerol is a simple polyol compound. Glycerol is sweet-tasting and of low toxicity.
/datum/reagent/glycerol.name: Glycerol

/datum/reagent/gold.desc: Gold is a dense, soft, shiny metal and the most malleable and ductile metal known.
/datum/reagent/gold.name: Gold

/datum/reagent/gondola_mutation_toxin.desc: A highly mutative liquid of unknown origin.
/datum/reagent/gondola_mutation_toxin.name: Tranquility

/datum/reagent/gondola_mutation_toxin/vi.desc: A highly mutative liquid of unknown origin.
/datum/reagent/gondola_mutation_toxin/vi.name: Tranquility

/datum/reagent/gravitum.desc: A rare kind of null fluid, capable of temporalily removing all weight of whatever it touches.
/datum/reagent/gravitum.name: Gravitum

/datum/reagent/growthserum.desc: A commercial chemical designed to help older men in the bedroom.
/datum/reagent/growthserum.name: Growth Serum

/datum/reagent/hair_dye.desc: Has a high chance of making you look like a mad scientist.
/datum/reagent/hair_dye.name: Quantum Hair Dye

/datum/reagent/halon.desc: A fire suppression gas that removes oxygen and cools down the area
/datum/reagent/halon.name: Halon

/datum/reagent/hauntium.desc: An eerie liquid created by purifying the prescence of ghosts. If it happens to get in your body, it starts hurting your soul.
/datum/reagent/hauntium.name: Hauntium

/datum/reagent/healium.desc: A powerful sleeping agent with healing properties
/datum/reagent/healium.name: Healium

/datum/reagent/hydrogen.desc: A colorless, odorless, nonmetallic, tasteless, highly combustible diatomic gas.
/datum/reagent/hydrogen.name: Hydrogen

/datum/reagent/hydrogen_peroxide.desc: An ubiquitous chemical substance that is composed of hydrogen and oxygen and oxygen.
/datum/reagent/hydrogen_peroxide.name: Hydrogen Peroxide

/datum/reagent/hypernoblium.desc: A suppressive gas that stops gas reactions on those who inhale it.
/datum/reagent/hypernoblium.name: Hyper-Noblium

/datum/reagent/impedrezene.desc: Impedrezene is a narcotic that impedes one's ability by slowing down the higher brain cell functions.
/datum/reagent/impedrezene.name: Impedrezene

/datum/reagent/impurity.desc: Impure chemical isomers made from inoptimal reactions. Causes mild liver damage
/datum/reagent/impurity.name: Chemical Isomers

/datum/reagent/impurity/aiuri.desc: This reagent is known to interfere with the eyesight of a patient.
/datum/reagent/impurity/aiuri.name: Aivime

/datum/reagent/impurity/chloralax.desc: An oily, colorless and slightly toxic liquid. It is produced when impure choral hydrate is broken down inside an organism.
/datum/reagent/impurity/chloralax.name: Chloralax

/datum/reagent/impurity/eigenswap.desc: This reagent is known to swap the handedness of a patient.
/datum/reagent/impurity/eigenswap.name: Eigenswap

/datum/reagent/impurity/healing.desc: Not all impure reagents are bad! Sometimes you might want to specifically make these!
/datum/reagent/impurity/healing.name: Healing Impure Reagent

/datum/reagent/impurity/healing/medicine.desc: A viscous mess of various medicines. Will heal a damage type at random
/datum/reagent/impurity/healing/medicine.name: Insolvent Medicinal Precipitate

/datum/reagent/impurity/inacusiate.desc: Makes the patient's hearing temporarily funky.
/datum/reagent/impurity/inacusiate.name: Tinacusiate

/datum/reagent/impurity/ipecacide.desc: An extremely gross substance that induces vomiting. It is produced when Lipolicide reactions are impure.
/datum/reagent/impurity/ipecacide.name: Ipecacide

/datum/reagent/impurity/lentslurri.desc: A highly addicitive muscle relaxant that is made when Lenturi reactions go wrong.
/datum/reagent/impurity/lentslurri.name: Lentslurri

/datum/reagent/impurity/libitoil.desc: Temporarilly interferes a patient's ability to process alcohol.
/datum/reagent/impurity/libitoil.name: Libitoil

/datum/reagent/impurity/mannitol.desc: Gives the patient a temporary speech impediment.
/datum/reagent/impurity/mannitol.name: Mannitoil

/datum/reagent/impurity/methanol.desc: A light, colourless liquid with a distinct smell. Ingestion can lead to blindness. It is a byproduct of organisms processing impure Formaldehyde.
/datum/reagent/impurity/methanol.name: Methanol

/datum/reagent/impurity/probital_failed.desc: This enzyme catalyzes crashes the conversion of nutricious food into healing peptides.
/datum/reagent/impurity/probital_failed.name: Metabolic Inhibition Factor

/datum/reagent/impurity/rosenol.desc: A strange, blue liquid that is produced during impure mindbreaker toxin reactions. Historically it has been abused to write poetry.
/datum/reagent/impurity/rosenol.name: Rosenol

/datum/reagent/inverse.desc: Inverse reagents are created when a reagent's purity is below it's inverse threshold. The are created either during ingestion - which will then replace their associated reagent, or some can be created during the reaction process.
/datum/reagent/inverse.name: Toxic Monomers

/datum/reagent/inverse/antihol.desc: Promotes alcoholic substances within the patients body, making their effects more potent.
/datum/reagent/inverse/antihol.name: Prohol

/datum/reagent/inverse/aranesp.desc: Synthetic medication that induces blood regeneration and wound clotting in patients.  Causes adverse side effects, including arterial damage and migraines when excessively used over time.
/datum/reagent/inverse/aranesp.name: Epoetin Alfa

/datum/reagent/inverse/baldium.desc: Potent psychotropic that causes intense anger within users.
/datum/reagent/inverse/baldium.name: Maldium

/datum/reagent/inverse/bath_salts.desc: Oop aak chee aak eek chee. Eek aak oop chee oop aak aak!!
/datum/reagent/inverse/bath_salts.name: Monkey Dust

/datum/reagent/inverse/colorful_reagent.desc: Extremely drab coloring pigment that is favored by corporations who wish to maximize suffering.
/datum/reagent/inverse/colorful_reagent.name: Dulling Reagent

/datum/reagent/inverse/corazargh.desc: Interferes with the body's natural pacemaker, forcing the patient to manually beat their heart.
/datum/reagent/inverse/corazargh.name: Corazargh

/datum/reagent/inverse/cryostylane.desc: Freezes the live or dead patient in a cryostasis ice block.
/datum/reagent/inverse/cryostylane.name: Cryogelidia

/datum/reagent/inverse/gravitum.desc: Experimental reagent that induces heavy gravokinetic effects on users.
/datum/reagent/inverse/gravitum.name: Newtonium

/datum/reagent/inverse/happiness.desc: Causes severe depressive behavior in users, and actively purges other antidepressants.
/datum/reagent/inverse/happiness.name: Sadness

/datum/reagent/inverse/healing.desc: Not all impure reagents are bad! Sometimes you might want to specifically make these!
/datum/reagent/inverse/healing.name: Healing Inverse Reagent

/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/convermol.desc: This reagent is known to coat the inside of a patient's lungs, providing greater protection against hot or cold air.
/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/convermol.name: Coveroli

/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/monover.desc: A toxin treating reagent, that only is effective if it's the only reagent present in the patient.
/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/monover.name: Monover

/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/syriniver.desc: This reagent reduces the impurity of all non medicines within the patient, reducing their negative effects.
/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/syriniver.name: Syrinifergus

/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/tirimol.desc: This will send the patient to sleep, adding a bonus to the efficacy of all reagents administered.
/datum/reagent/inverse/healing/tirimol.name: Super Melatonin

/datum/reagent/inverse/helgrasp.desc: This rare and forbidden concoction is thought to bring you closer to the grasp of the Norse goddess Hel.
/datum/reagent/inverse/helgrasp.name: Helgrasp

/datum/reagent/inverse/helgrasp/heretic.desc: The Hand of the Mansus is at your neck.
/datum/reagent/inverse/helgrasp/heretic.name: Grasp of the Mansus

/datum/reagent/inverse/hercuri.desc: This reagent causes a dramatic raise in the patient's body temperature. Overdosing makes the effect even stronger and causes severe liver damage.
/datum/reagent/inverse/hercuri.name: Herignis

/datum/reagent/inverse/ichiyuri.desc: Prolonged exposure to this chemical can cause an overwhelming urge to itch oneself.
/datum/reagent/inverse/ichiyuri.name: Ichiyuri

/datum/reagent/inverse/krokodil.desc: Highly potent sedative that provides the best benefits for pain management and surgery. Extremely addictive.
/datum/reagent/inverse/krokodil.name: Permonid

/datum/reagent/inverse/neurine.desc: Induces a temporary brain trauma in the patient by redirecting neuron activity.
/datum/reagent/inverse/neurine.name: Neruwhine

/datum/reagent/inverse/penthrite.desc: A reagent that is known to stimulate the heart in a dead patient, temporarily bringing back recently dead patients at great cost to their heart. Mildly toxic when inert in a patient.
/datum/reagent/inverse/penthrite.name: Nooartrium

/datum/reagent/inverse/technetium.desc: A radioactive tracer agent that can improve a scanner's ability to detect internal organ damage. Will poison the patient when present very slowly, purging or using a low dose is recommended after use.
/datum/reagent/inverse/technetium.name: Technetium 99

/datum/reagent/iodine.desc: Commonly added to table salt as a nutrient. On its own it tastes far less pleasing.
/datum/reagent/iodine.name: Iodine

/datum/reagent/kronkus_extract.desc: A frothy extract made from fermented kronkus vine pulp.\nHighly bitter due to the presence of a variety of kronkamines.
/datum/reagent/kronkus_extract.name: Kronkus Extract

/datum/reagent/lead.desc: A dull metalltic element with a low melting point.
/datum/reagent/lead.name: Lead

/datum/reagent/liquid_dark_matter.desc: Sucks everything into the detonation point.
/datum/reagent/liquid_dark_matter.name: Liquid Dark Matter

/datum/reagent/liquid_justice.desc: Rumors say that only the truly robust can safelly process this chemical
/datum/reagent/liquid_justice.name: Liquid justice

/datum/reagent/lithium.desc: A silver metal, its claim to fame is its remarkably low density. Using it is a bit too effective in calming oneself down.
/datum/reagent/lithium.name: Lithium

/datum/reagent/love.desc: This food's been made... with love.
/datum/reagent/love.name: Love

/datum/reagent/lube.desc: Lubricant is a substance introduced between two moving surfaces to reduce the friction and wear between them. giggity.
/datum/reagent/lube.name: Space Lube

/datum/reagent/lube/superlube.desc: This \[REDACTED\] has been outlawed after the incident on \[DATA EXPUNGED\].
/datum/reagent/lube/superlube.name: Super Duper Lube

/datum/reagent/lye.desc: Also known as sodium hydroxide. As a profession making this is somewhat underwhelming.
/datum/reagent/lye.name: Lye

/datum/reagent/magillitis.desc: An experimental serum which causes rapid muscular growth in Hominidae. Side-affects may include hypertrichosis, violent outbursts, and an unending affinity for bananas.
/datum/reagent/magillitis.name: Magillitis

/datum/reagent/medicine/adminordrazine.desc: It's magic. We don't have to explain it.
/datum/reagent/medicine/adminordrazine.name: Adminordrazine

/datum/reagent/medicine/adminordrazine/q.desc: Rare and experimental particles, that apparently swap the user's body with one from an alternate dimension where it's completely healthy.
/datum/reagent/medicine/adminordrazine/q.name: Quantum Medicine

/datum/reagent/medicine/ammoniated_mercu.desc: Quickly purges the body of toxic chemicals. Heals toxin damage when in a good condition someone has  		no brute and fire damage. When hurt with brute or fire damage, it can deal a great amount of toxin damage.  When there are no toxins present, it starts slowly purging itself.
/datum/reagent/medicine/ammoniated_mercu.name: Ammoniated Mercury

/datum/reagent/medicine/antihol.desc: Purges alcoholic substance from the patient's body and eliminates its side effects.
/datum/reagent/medicine/antihol.name: Antihol

/datum/reagent/medicine/atropine.desc: If a patient is in critical condition, rapidly heals all damage types as well as regulating oxygen in the body. Excellent for stabilizing wounded patients, and said to neutralize blood-activated internal explosives found amongst clandestine black op agents.
/datum/reagent/medicine/atropine.name: Atropine

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/aiuri.desc: Used to treat burns. Does minor eye damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/aiuri.name: Aiuri

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/convermol.desc: Restores oxygen deprivation while producing a lesser amount of toxic byproducts. Both scale with exposure to the drug and current amount of oxygen deprivation. Overdose causes toxic byproducts regardless of oxygen deprivation.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/convermol.name: Convermol

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/helbital.desc: Named after the norse goddess Hel, this medicine heals the patient's bruises the closer they are to death. Patients will find the medicine 'aids' their healing if not near death by causing asphyxiation.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/helbital.name: Helbital

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/hercuri.desc: Not to be confused with element Mercury, this medicine excels in reverting effects of dangerous high-temperature environments. Prolonged exposure can cause hypothermia.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/hercuri.name: Hercuri

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/lenturi.desc: Used to treat burns. Makes you move slower while it is in your system. Applies stomach damage when it leaves your system.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/lenturi.name: Lenturi

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/libital.desc: A bruise reliever. Does minor liver damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/libital.name: Libital

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/multiver.desc: A chem-purger that becomes more effective the more unique medicines present. Slightly heals toxicity but causes lung damage (mitigatable by unique medicines).
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/multiver.name: Multiver

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/musiver.desc: The active metabolite of syriniver. Causes muscle weakness on overdose
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/musiver.name: Musiver

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/penthrite.desc: An expensive medicine that aids with pumping blood around the body even without a heart, and prevents the heart from slowing down. Mixing it with epinephrine or atropine will cause an explosion.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/penthrite.name: Penthrite

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/probital.desc: Originally developed as a prototype-gym supliment for those looking for quick workout turnover, this oral medication quickly repairs broken muscle tissue but causes lactic acid buildup, tiring the patient. Overdosing can cause extreme drowsiness. An Influx of nutrients promotes the muscle repair even further.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/probital.name: Probital

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/seiver.desc: A medicine that shifts functionality based on temperature. Hotter temperatures will heal more toxicity, while colder temperatures will heal larger amounts of toxicity but only while the patient is irradiated. Damages the heart.

dyn.cond: radcalc > 0 && has TRAIT_IRRADIATED; else, chemtemp < rads_heal_threshold

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/seiver.name: Seiver

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/synthflesh.desc: Heals brute and burn damage at the cost of toxicity (66% of damage healed). 100u or more can restore corpses husked by burns. Touch application only.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/synthflesh.name: Synthflesh

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/synthflesh/bi.desc: A weaker, biological version of synthflesh that heals brute and burn, at the cost of causing more toxin damage, and being unable to unhusk. Touch application only.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/synthflesh/bi.name: Biocellulose

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/syriniver.desc: A potent antidote for intravenous use with a narrow therapeutic index, it is considered an active prodrug of musiver.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/syriniver.name: Syriniver

/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/tirimol.desc: An oxygen deprivation medication that causes fatigue. Prolonged exposure causes the patient to fall asleep once the medicine metabolizes.
/datum/reagent/medicine/c2/tirimol.name: Tirimol

/datum/reagent/medicine/calomel.desc: Quickly purges the body of all chemicals except itself. The more health a person has,  the more toxin damage it will deal. It can heal toxin damage when people have low enough health.
/datum/reagent/medicine/calomel.name: Calomel

/datum/reagent/medicine/changelinghaste.desc: Drastically increases movement speed, but deals toxin damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/changelinghaste.name: Changeling Haste

/datum/reagent/medicine/clonexadone.desc: A chemical that derives from Cryoxadone. It specializes in healing clone damage, but nothing else. Requires very cold temperatures to properly metabolize, and metabolizes quicker than cryoxadone.
/datum/reagent/medicine/clonexadone.name: Clonexadone

/datum/reagent/medicine/coagulant.desc: A proprietary coagulant used to help bleeding wounds clot faster. It is purged by heparin.
/datum/reagent/medicine/coagulant.name: Sanguirite

/datum/reagent/medicine/coagulant/banana.desc: Ancient Clown Lore says that pulped banana peels are good for your blood, but are you really going to take medical advice from a clown about bananas?
/datum/reagent/medicine/coagulant/banana.name: Pulped Banana Peel

/datum/reagent/medicine/coagulant/seraka.desc: A deeply coloured oil present in small amounts in Seraka Mushrooms. Acts as an effective blood clotting agent, but has a low overdose threshold.
/datum/reagent/medicine/coagulant/seraka.name: Seraka Extract

/datum/reagent/medicine/cordiolis_hepati.desc: A strange, pitch-black reagent that seems to absorb all light. Effects unknown.
/datum/reagent/medicine/cordiolis_hepati.name: Cordiolis Hepatico

/datum/reagent/medicine/cryoxadone.desc: A chemical mixture with almost magical healing powers. Its main limitation is that the patient's body temperature must be under 270K for it to metabolise correctly.
/datum/reagent/medicine/cryoxadone.name: Cryoxadone

/datum/reagent/medicine/diphenhydramine.desc: Rapidly purges the body of Histamine and reduces jitteriness. Slight chance of causing drowsiness.
/datum/reagent/medicine/diphenhydramine.name: Diphenhydramine

/datum/reagent/medicine/earthsblood.desc: Ichor from an extremely powerful plant. Great for restoring wounds, but it's a little heavy on the brain. For some strange reason, it also induces temporary pacifism in those who imbibe it and semi-permanent pacifism in those who overdose on it.
/datum/reagent/medicine/earthsblood.name: Earthsblood

/datum/reagent/medicine/ephedrine.desc: Increases resistance to batons and movement speed, giving you hand cramps. Overdose deals toxin damage and inhibits breathing.
/datum/reagent/medicine/ephedrine.name: Ephedrine

/datum/reagent/medicine/epinephrine.desc: Very minor boost to stun resistance. Slowly heals damage if a patient is in critical condition, as well as regulating oxygen loss. Overdose causes weakness and toxin damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/epinephrine.name: Epinephrine

/datum/reagent/medicine/granibitaluri.desc: A mild painkiller useful as an additive alongside more potent medicines. Speeds up the healing of small wounds and burns, but is ineffective at treating severe injuries. Extremely large doses are toxic, and may eventually cause liver failure.
/datum/reagent/medicine/granibitaluri.name: Granibitaluri

/datum/reagent/medicine/haloperidol.desc: Increases depletion rates for most stimulating/hallucinogenic drugs. Reduces druggy effects and jitteriness. Severe stamina regeneration penalty, causes drowsiness. Small chance of brain damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/haloperidol.name: Haloperidol

/datum/reagent/medicine/higadrite.desc: A medication utilized to treat ailing livers.
/datum/reagent/medicine/higadrite.name: Higadrite

/datum/reagent/medicine/inacusiate.desc: Rapidly repairs damage to the patient's ears to cure deafness, assuming the source of said deafness isn't from genetic mutations, chronic deafness, or a total defecit of ears.
/datum/reagent/medicine/inacusiate.name: Inacusiate

/datum/reagent/medicine/inaprovaline.desc: Stabilizes the breathing of patients. Good for those in critical condition.
/datum/reagent/medicine/inaprovaline.name: Inaprovaline

/datum/reagent/medicine/leporazine.desc: Leporazine will effectively regulate a patient's body temperature, ensuring it never leaves safe levels.
/datum/reagent/medicine/leporazine.name: Leporazine

/datum/reagent/medicine/metafactor.desc: This enzyme catalyzes the conversion of nutricious food into healing peptides.
/datum/reagent/medicine/metafactor.name: Mitogen Metabolism Factor

/datum/reagent/medicine/mine_salve.desc: A powerful painkiller. Restores bruising and burns in addition to making the patient believe they are fully healed. Also great for treating severe burn wounds in a pinch.
/datum/reagent/medicine/mine_salve.name: Miner's Salve

/datum/reagent/medicine/modafinil.desc: Long-lasting sleep suppressant that very slightly reduces stun and knockdown times. Overdosing has horrendous side effects and deals lethal oxygen damage, will knock you unconscious if not dealt with.
/datum/reagent/medicine/modafinil.name: Modafinil

/datum/reagent/medicine/muscle_stimulant.desc: A potent chemical that allows someone under its influence to be at full physical ability even when under massive amounts of pain.
/datum/reagent/medicine/muscle_stimulant.name: Muscle Stimulant

/datum/reagent/medicine/mutadone.desc: Removes jitteriness and restores genetic defects.
/datum/reagent/medicine/mutadone.name: Mutadone

/datum/reagent/medicine/naloxone.desc: Opioid antagonist that purges drowsiness and narcotics from the patient, restores breath loss and accelerates addiction recovery.
/datum/reagent/medicine/naloxone.name: Naloxone

/datum/reagent/medicine/neurine.desc: Reacts with neural tissue, helping reform damaged connections. Can cure minor traumas.
/datum/reagent/medicine/neurine.name: Neurine

/datum/reagent/medicine/oculine.desc: Quickly restores eye damage, cures nearsightedness, and has a chance to restore vision to the blind.

/datum/reagent/medicine/oculine.name: Oculine

/datum/reagent/medicine/omnizine.desc: Slowly heals all damage types. Overdose will cause damage in all types instead.
/datum/reagent/medicine/omnizine.name: Omnizine

/datum/reagent/medicine/omnizine/godbloo.desc: Slowly heals all damage types. Has a rather high overdose threshold. Glows with mysterious power.
/datum/reagent/medicine/omnizine/godbloo.name: Godblood

/datum/reagent/medicine/omnizine/protozi.desc: A less environmentally friendly and somewhat weaker variant of omnizine.
/datum/reagent/medicine/omnizine/protozi.name: Protozine

/datum/reagent/medicine/oxandrolone.desc: stimulates the healing of severe burns. Extremely rapidly heals severe burns and slowly heals minor ones. Overdose will worsen existing burns.
/datum/reagent/medicine/oxandrolone.name: Oxandrolone

/datum/reagent/medicine/painkiller/morph.desc: A painkiller that allows the patient to move at full speed even when injured. Causes drowsiness and eventually unconsciousness in high doses. Overdose will cause a variety of effects, ranging from minor to lethal.
/datum/reagent/medicine/painkiller/morph.name: Morphine

/datum/reagent/medicine/painkiller/robop.desc: Reduces the stimulus response capacity of positronic systems, anesthetizing, soothing, and in high doses, rendering them unconcious.
/datum/reagent/medicine/painkiller/robop.name: Positronic Neural Dampener

/datum/reagent/medicine/pen_acid.desc: Reduces massive amounts of toxin damage while purging other chemicals from the body.
/datum/reagent/medicine/pen_acid.name: Pentetic Acid

/datum/reagent/medicine/polypyr.desc: A purple mixture of short polyelectrolyte chains not easily synthesized in the laboratory. It is valued as an intermediate in the synthesis of the cutting edge pharmaceuticals.
/datum/reagent/medicine/polypyr.name: Polypyrylium Oligomers

/datum/reagent/medicine/potass_iodide.desc: Heals low toxin damage while the patient is irradiated, and will halt the damaging effects of radiation. Can be used to decontaminate irradiated items.
/datum/reagent/medicine/potass_iodide.name: Potassium Iodide

/datum/reagent/medicine/psicodine.desc: Suppresses anxiety and other various forms of mental distress. Overdose causes hallucinations and minor toxin damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/psicodine.name: Psicodine

/datum/reagent/medicine/pyroxadone.desc: A mixture of cryoxadone and slime jelly, that apparently inverses the requirement for its activation.
/datum/reagent/medicine/pyroxadone.name: Pyroxadone

/datum/reagent/medicine/regen_jelly.desc: Gradually regenerates all types of damage, without harming slime anatomy.
/datum/reagent/medicine/regen_jelly.name: Regenerative Jelly

/datum/reagent/medicine/regen_jelly/weak.desc: Artificially weakened regenerative slime jelly that regenerates tissues slower, but lasts longer with the same volume.
/datum/reagent/medicine/regen_jelly/weak.name: Weakened Regenerative Jelly

/datum/reagent/medicine/rezadone.desc: A powder derived from fish toxin, Rezadone can effectively treat genetic damage as well as restoring minor wounds and restoring corpses husked by burns. Overdose will cause intense nausea and minor toxin damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/rezadone.name: Rezadone

/datum/reagent/medicine/sal_acid.desc: stimulates the healing of severe bruises. Extremely rapidly heals severe bruising and slowly heals minor ones. Overdose will worsen existing bruising.
/datum/reagent/medicine/sal_acid.name: Salicylic Acid

/datum/reagent/medicine/salbutamol.desc: Rapidly restores oxygen deprivation as well as preventing more of it to an extent.
/datum/reagent/medicine/salbutamol.name: Salbutamol

/datum/reagent/medicine/salglu_solution.desc: Has a 33% chance per metabolism cycle to heal brute and burn damage. Can be used as a temporary blood substitute, as well as slowly speeding blood regeneration.
/datum/reagent/medicine/salglu_solution.name: Saline-Glucose Solution

/datum/reagent/medicine/silibinin.desc: A thistle derrived hepatoprotective flavolignan mixture that help reverse damage to the liver.
/datum/reagent/medicine/silibinin.name: Silibinin

/datum/reagent/medicine/stimulants.desc: Increases resistance to batons and movement speed in addition to restoring minor damage and weakness. Overdose causes weakness and toxin damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/stimulants.name: Stimulants

/datum/reagent/medicine/strange_reagent.desc: A miracle drug capable of bringing the dead back to life. Works topically unless anotamically complex, in which case works orally. Cannot revive targets under -%MAXHEALTHRATIO% health.
/datum/reagent/medicine/strange_reagent.name: Strange Reagent

/datum/reagent/medicine/strange_reagent/.desc: A miracle drug capable of bringing the dead back to life. Works topically unless anotamically complex, in which case works orally. Cannot revive targets under -%MAXHEALTHRATIO% health.
/datum/reagent/medicine/strange_reagent/.name: Stranger Reagent

/datum/reagent/medicine/synaphydramine.desc: Reduces drowsiness, hallucinations, and Histamine from body.
/datum/reagent/medicine/synaphydramine.name: Diphen-Synaptizine

/datum/reagent/medicine/synaptizine.desc: Increases resistance to stuns as well as reducing drowsiness and hallucinations.
/datum/reagent/medicine/synaptizine.name: Synaptizine

/datum/reagent/medicine/synaptizine/syna.desc: Increases resistance to stuns as well as reducing drowsiness and hallucinations.
/datum/reagent/medicine/synaptizine/syna.name: Virus Rations

/datum/reagent/medicine/syndicate_nanite.desc: Miniature medical robots that swiftly restore bodily damage.
/datum/reagent/medicine/syndicate_nanite.name: Restorative Nanites

/datum/reagent/mercury.desc: A curious metal that's a liquid at room temperature. Neurodegenerative and very bad for the mind.
/datum/reagent/mercury.name: Mercury

/datum/reagent/metalgen.desc: A purple metal morphic liquid, said to impose it's metallic properties on whatever it touches.
/datum/reagent/metalgen.name: Metalgen

/datum/reagent/mulligan.desc: This toxin will rapidly change the DNA of humanoid beings. Commonly used by Syndicate spies and assassins in need of an emergency ID change.
/datum/reagent/mulligan.name: Mulligan Toxin

/datum/reagent/nitrium_high_metabolizati.desc: A highly reactive byproduct that stops you from sleeping, while dealing increasing toxin damage over time.
/datum/reagent/nitrium_high_metabolizati.name: Nitrosyl plasmide

/datum/reagent/nitrium_low_metabolizatio.desc: A highly reactive gas that makes you feel faster.
/datum/reagent/nitrium_low_metabolizatio.name: Nitrium

/datum/reagent/nitrogen.desc: A colorless, odorless, tasteless gas. A simple asphyxiant that can silently displace vital oxygen.
/datum/reagent/nitrogen.name: Nitrogen

/datum/reagent/nitroglycerin.desc: Nitroglycerin is a heavy, colorless, oily, explosive liquid obtained by nitrating glycerol.
/datum/reagent/nitroglycerin.name: Nitroglycerin

/datum/reagent/nitrous_oxide.desc: A potent oxidizer used as fuel in rockets and as an anaesthetic during surgery. As it is an anticoagulant, nitrous oxide is best  used alongside sanguirite to allow blood clotting to continue.
/datum/reagent/nitrous_oxide.name: Nitrous Oxide

/datum/reagent/oxygen.desc: A colorless, odorless gas. Grows on trees but is still pretty valuable.
/datum/reagent/oxygen.name: Oxygen

/datum/reagent/pax.desc: A colorless liquid that suppresses violence in its subjects.
/datum/reagent/pax.name: Pax

/datum/reagent/pax/peaceborg.desc: A colorless liquid that suppresses violence in its subjects. Cheaper to synthesize than normal Pax, but wears off faster.
/datum/reagent/pax/peaceborg.name: Synthpax

/datum/reagent/peaceborg/confuse.desc: Makes the target off balance and dizzy
/datum/reagent/peaceborg/confuse.name: Dizzying Solution

/datum/reagent/peaceborg/tire.desc: An extremely weak stamina-toxin that tires out the target. Completely harmless.
/datum/reagent/peaceborg/tire.name: Tiring Solution

/datum/reagent/pentaerythritol.desc: Slow down, it ain't no spelling bee!
/datum/reagent/pentaerythritol.name: Pentaerythritol

/datum/reagent/peptides_failed.desc: These inhibitory peptides cause cellular damage and cost nutrition to the patient!
/datum/reagent/peptides_failed.name: Prion Peptides

/datum/reagent/phenol.desc: An aromatic ring of carbon with a hydroxyl group. A useful precursor to some medicines, but has no healing properties on its own.
/datum/reagent/phenol.name: Phenol

/datum/reagent/phlogiston.desc: Catches you on fire and makes you ignite.
/datum/reagent/phlogiston.name: Phlogiston

/datum/reagent/phosphorus.desc: A ruddy red powder that burns readily. Though it comes in many colors, the general theme is always the same.
/datum/reagent/phosphorus.name: Phosphorus

/datum/reagent/plantnutriment.desc: Some kind of nutriment. You can't really tell what it is. You should probably report it, along with how you obtained it.
/datum/reagent/plantnutriment.name: Generic Nutriment

/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/endurogrow.desc: A specialized nutriment, which decreases product quantity and potency, but strengthens the plants endurance.
/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/endurogrow.name: Enduro Grow

/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/eznutrimen.desc: Contains electrolytes. It's what plants crave. It makes plants slowly gain potency and yield
/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/eznutrimen.name: E-Z Nutrient

/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/left4zednu.desc: Unstable nutriment that makes plants wilt quickly but increases all stats while doing so.
/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/left4zednu.name: Left 4 Zed

/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/liquideart.desc: A specialized nutriment, which increases the plant's production speed, as well as it's susceptibility to weeds.
/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/liquideart.name: Liquid Earthquake

/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/robustharv.desc: Very potent nutriment that slows plants from mutating whilst also making them grow faster.
/datum/reagent/plantnutriment/robustharv.name: Robust Harvest

/datum/reagent/plasma_oxide.desc: Compound created deep in the cores of demon-class planets. Commonly found through deep geysers.
/datum/reagent/plasma_oxide.name: Hyper-Plasmium Oxide

/datum/reagent/plastic_polymers.desc: the petroleum based components of plastic.
/datum/reagent/plastic_polymers.name: Plastic Polymers

/datum/reagent/pluoxium.desc: A gas that is eight times more efficient than O2 at lung diffusion with organ healing properties on sleeping patients.
/datum/reagent/pluoxium.name: Pluoxium

/datum/reagent/potassium.desc: A soft, low-melting solid that can easily be cut with a knife. Reacts violently with water.
/datum/reagent/potassium.name: Potassium

/datum/reagent/prefactor_a.desc: This reagent is a prefactor to the purity tester reagent, and will react with stable plasma to create it
/datum/reagent/prefactor_a.name: Interim Product Alpha

/datum/reagent/prefactor_b.desc: This reagent is a prefactor to the reaction speed agent reagent, and will react with stable plasma to create it
/datum/reagent/prefactor_b.name: Interim Product Beta

/datum/reagent/pyrosium.desc: Comes into existence at 20K. As long as there is sufficient oxygen for it to react with, Pyrosium slowly heats all other reagents in the container.
/datum/reagent/pyrosium.name: Pyrosium

/datum/reagent/reaction_agent.desc: Hello! I am a bugged reagent. Please report me for my crimes. Thank you!!
/datum/reagent/reaction_agent.name: Reaction Agent

/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/acidic_buf.desc: This reagent will consume itself and move the pH of a beaker towards acidity when added to another.
/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/acidic_buf.name: Strong Acidic Buffer

/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/basic_buff.desc: This reagent will consume itself and move the pH of a beaker towards alkalinity when added to another.
/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/basic_buff.name: Strong Basic Buffer

/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/purity_tes.desc: This reagent will consume itself and violently react if there is a highly impure reagent in the beaker.
/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/purity_tes.name: Purity Tester

/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/speed_agen.desc: This reagent will consume itself and speed up an ongoing reaction, modifying the current reaction's purity by it's own.
/datum/reagent/reaction_agent/speed_agen.name: Tempomyocin

/datum/reagent/romerol.desc: Romerol is a highly experimental bioterror agent  		which causes dormant nodules to be etched into the grey matter of  		the subject. These nodules only become active upon death of the  		host, upon which, the secondary structures activate and take control  of the host body.
/datum/reagent/romerol.name: Romerol

/datum/reagent/royal_bee_jelly.desc: Royal Bee Jelly, if injected into a Queen Space Bee said bee will split into two bees.
/datum/reagent/royal_bee_jelly.name: Royal Bee Jelly

/datum/reagent/serotrotium.desc: A chemical compound that promotes concentrated production of the serotonin neurotransmitter in humans.
/datum/reagent/serotrotium.name: Serotrotium

/datum/reagent/silicon.desc: A tetravalent metalloid, silicon is less reactive than its chemical analog carbon.
/datum/reagent/silicon.name: Silicon

/datum/reagent/silver.desc: A soft, white, lustrous transition metal, it has the highest electrical conductivity of any element and the highest thermal conductivity of any metal.
/datum/reagent/silver.name: Silver

/datum/reagent/smart_foaming_agent.desc: An agent that yields metallic foam which conforms to area boundaries when mixed with light metal and a strong acid.
/datum/reagent/smart_foaming_agent.name: Smart Foaming Agent

/datum/reagent/smoke_powder.desc: Makes a large cloud of smoke that can carry reagents.
/datum/reagent/smoke_powder.name: Smoke Powder

/datum/reagent/snail.desc: Virological agent that infects the subject with Gastrolosis.
/datum/reagent/snail.name: Agent-S

/datum/reagent/sodium.desc: A soft silver metal that can easily be cut with a knife. It's not salt just yet, so refrain from putting it on your chips.
/datum/reagent/sodium.name: Sodium

/datum/reagent/sorium.desc: Sends everything flying from the detonation point.
/datum/reagent/sorium.name: Sorium

/datum/reagent/space_cleaner.desc: A compound used to clean things. Now with 50% more sodium hypochlorite! Can be used to clean wounds, but it's not really meant for that.
/datum/reagent/space_cleaner.name: Space Cleaner

/datum/reagent/space_cleaner/ez_clean.desc: A powerful, acidic cleaner sold by Waffle Co. Affects organic matter while leaving other objects unaffected.
/datum/reagent/space_cleaner/ez_clean.name: EZ Clean

/datum/reagent/space_cleaner/sterilizine.desc: Sterilizes wounds in preparation for surgery.
/datum/reagent/space_cleaner/sterilizine.name: Sterilizine

/datum/reagent/spider_extract.desc: A highly specialized extract coming from the Australicus sector, used to create broodmother spiders.
/datum/reagent/spider_extract.name: Spider Extract

/datum/reagent/spraytan.desc: A substance applied to the skin to darken the skin.
/datum/reagent/spraytan.name: Spray Tan

/datum/reagent/stabilizing_agent.desc: Keeps unstable chemicals stable. This does not work on everything.
/datum/reagent/stabilizing_agent.name: Stabilizing Agent

/datum/reagent/stable_plasma.desc: Non-flammable plasma locked into a liquid form that cannot ignite or become gaseous/solid.
/datum/reagent/stable_plasma.name: Stable Plasma

/datum/reagent/sulfur.desc: A sickly yellow solid mostly known for its nasty smell. It's actually much more helpful than it looks in biochemisty.
/datum/reagent/sulfur.name: Sulfur

/datum/reagent/teslium.desc: An unstable, electrically-charged metallic slurry. Periodically electrocutes its victim, and makes electrocutions against them more deadly. Excessively heating teslium results in dangerous destabilization. Do not allow to come into contact with water.
/datum/reagent/teslium.name: Teslium

/datum/reagent/teslium/energized_jelly.desc: Electrically-charged jelly. Boosts jellypeople's nervous system, but only shocks other lifeforms.
/datum/reagent/teslium/energized_jelly.name: Energized Jelly

/datum/reagent/thermite.desc: Thermite produces an aluminothermic reaction known as a thermite reaction. Can be used to melt walls.
/datum/reagent/thermite.name: Thermite

/datum/reagent/toxin/acid.desc: A strong mineral acid with the molecular formula H2SO4.
/datum/reagent/toxin/acid.name: Sulfuric Acid

/datum/reagent/toxin/acid/fluacid.desc: Fluorosulfuric acid is an extremely corrosive chemical substance.
/datum/reagent/toxin/acid/fluacid.name: Fluorosulfuric Acid

/datum/reagent/toxin/acid/nitracid.desc: Nitric acid is an extremely corrosive chemical substance that violently reacts with living organic tissue.
/datum/reagent/toxin/acid/nitracid.name: Nitric Acid

/datum/reagent/toxin/amanitin.desc: A very powerful delayed toxin. Upon full metabolization, a massive amount of toxin damage will be dealt depending on how long it has been in the victim's bloodstream.
/datum/reagent/toxin/amanitin.name: Amanitin

/datum/reagent/toxin/amatoxin.desc: A powerful poison derived from certain species of mushroom.
/datum/reagent/toxin/amatoxin.name: Amatoxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/anacea.desc: A toxin that quickly purges medicines and metabolizes very slowly.
/datum/reagent/toxin/anacea.name: Anacea

/datum/reagent/toxin/bad_food.desc: The result of some abomination of cookery, food so bad it's toxic.
/datum/reagent/toxin/bad_food.name: Bad Food

/datum/reagent/toxin/bonehurtingjuice.desc: A strange substance that looks a lot like water. Drinking it is oddly tempting. Oof ouch.
/datum/reagent/toxin/bonehurtingjuice.name: Bone Hurting Juice

/datum/reagent/toxin/bungotoxin.desc: A horrible cardiotoxin that protects the humble bungo pit.
/datum/reagent/toxin/bungotoxin.name: Bungotoxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/carpotoxin.desc: A deadly neurotoxin produced by the dreaded spess carp.
/datum/reagent/toxin/carpotoxin.name: Carpotoxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/chloralhydrate.desc: A powerful sedative that induces confusion and drowsiness before putting its target to sleep.
/datum/reagent/toxin/chloralhydrate.name: Chloral Hydrate

/datum/reagent/toxin/coffeepowder.desc: Finely ground coffee beans, used to make coffee.
/datum/reagent/toxin/coffeepowder.name: Coffee Grounds

/datum/reagent/toxin/coniine.desc: Coniine metabolizes extremely slowly, but deals high amounts of toxin damage and stops breathing.
/datum/reagent/toxin/coniine.name: Coniine

/datum/reagent/toxin/curare.desc: Causes slight toxin damage followed by chain-stunning and oxygen damage.
/datum/reagent/toxin/curare.name: Curare

/datum/reagent/toxin/cyanide.desc: An infamous poison known for its use in assassination. Causes small amounts of toxin damage with a small chance of oxygen damage or a stun.
/datum/reagent/toxin/cyanide.name: Cyanide

/datum/reagent/toxin/delayed.desc: Causes heavy toxin damage after a brief time of inactivity.
/datum/reagent/toxin/delayed.name: Toxin Microcapsules

/datum/reagent/toxin/fakebeer.desc: A specially-engineered sedative disguised as beer. It induces instant sleep in its target.
/datum/reagent/toxin/fakebeer.name: B33r

/datum/reagent/toxin/fentanyl.desc: Fentanyl will inhibit brain function and cause toxin damage before eventually knocking out its victim.
/datum/reagent/toxin/fentanyl.name: Fentanyl

/datum/reagent/toxin/formaldehyde.desc: Formaldehyde, on its own, is a fairly weak toxin. It contains trace amounts of Histamine. When used in a dead body, will prevent organ decay.
/datum/reagent/toxin/formaldehyde.name: Formaldehyde

/datum/reagent/toxin/ghoulpowder.desc: A strong neurotoxin that slows metabolism to a death-like state, while keeping the patient fully active. Causes toxin buildup if used too long.
/datum/reagent/toxin/ghoulpowder.name: Ghoul Powder

/datum/reagent/toxin/heparin.desc: A powerful anticoagulant. All open cut wounds on the victim will open up and bleed much faster. It directly purges sanguirite, a coagulant.
/datum/reagent/toxin/heparin.name: Heparin

/datum/reagent/toxin/histamine.desc: Histamine's effects become more dangerous depending on the dosage amount. They range from mildly annoying to incredibly lethal.
/datum/reagent/toxin/histamine.name: Histamine

/datum/reagent/toxin/hot_ice.desc: Frozen plasma, worth its weight in gold, to the right people.
/datum/reagent/toxin/hot_ice.name: Hot Ice Slush

/datum/reagent/toxin/hunterspider.desc: A toxic chemical produced by spiders to weaken prey.
/datum/reagent/toxin/hunterspider.name: Spider Toxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/initropidril.desc: A powerful poison with insidious effects. It can cause stuns, lethal breathing failure, and cardiac arrest.
/datum/reagent/toxin/initropidril.name: Initropidril

/datum/reagent/toxin/itching_powder.desc: A powder that induces itching upon contact with the skin. Causes the victim to scratch at their itches and has a very low chance to decay into Histamine.
/datum/reagent/toxin/itching_powder.name: Itching Powder

/datum/reagent/toxin/leadacetate.desc: Used hundreds of years ago as a sweetener, before it was realized that it's incredibly poisonous.
/datum/reagent/toxin/leadacetate.name: Lead Acetate

/datum/reagent/toxin/lexorin.desc: A powerful poison used to stop respiration.
/datum/reagent/toxin/lexorin.name: Lexorin

/datum/reagent/toxin/lipolicide.desc: A powerful toxin that will destroy fat cells, massively reducing body weight in a short time. Deadly to those without nutriment in their body.
/datum/reagent/toxin/lipolicide.name: Lipolicide

/datum/reagent/toxin/mimesbane.desc: A nonlethal neurotoxin that interferes with the victim's ability to gesture.
/datum/reagent/toxin/mimesbane.name: Mime's Bane

/datum/reagent/toxin/mindbreaker.desc: A powerful hallucinogen. Not a thing to be messed with. For some mental patients. it counteracts their symptoms and anchors them to reality.
/datum/reagent/toxin/mindbreaker.name: Mindbreaker Toxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/morbital.desc: A strange blood red substance that makes your skin crawl.
/datum/reagent/toxin/morbital.name: Morbital

/datum/reagent/toxin/mushroom_powder.desc: Finely ground polypore mushrooms, ready to be steeped in water to make mushroom tea.
/datum/reagent/toxin/mushroom_powder.name: Mushroom Powder

/datum/reagent/toxin/mutagen.desc: Might cause unpredictable mutations. Keep away from children.
/datum/reagent/toxin/mutagen.name: Unstable Mutagen

/datum/reagent/toxin/mutagen/mutagenviru.desc: Might cause unpredictable mutations. Keep away from children.
/datum/reagent/toxin/mutagen/mutagenviru.name: Mutagenic Agar

/datum/reagent/toxin/mutagen/mutagenviru.desc: Might cause unpredictable mutations. Keep away from children.
/datum/reagent/toxin/mutagen/mutagenviru.name: Sucrose Agar

/datum/reagent/toxin/mutetoxin.desc: A nonlethal poison that inhibits speech in its victim.
/datum/reagent/toxin/mutetoxin.name: Mute Toxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/pancuronium.desc: An undetectable toxin that swiftly incapacitates its victim. May also cause breathing failure.
/datum/reagent/toxin/pancuronium.name: Pancuronium

/datum/reagent/toxin/pestkiller.desc: A harmful toxic mixture to kill pests. Do not ingest!
/datum/reagent/toxin/pestkiller.name: Pest Killer

/datum/reagent/toxin/pestkiller/organic.desc: An organic mixture used to kill pests, with less of the side effects. Do not ingest!
/datum/reagent/toxin/pestkiller/organic.name: Natural Pest Killer

/datum/reagent/toxin/plantbgone.desc: A harmful toxic mixture to kill plantlife. Do not ingest!
/datum/reagent/toxin/plantbgone.name: Plant-B-Gone

/datum/reagent/toxin/plantbgone/weedkill.desc: A harmful toxic mixture to kill weeds. Do not ingest!
/datum/reagent/toxin/plantbgone/weedkill.name: Weed Killer

/datum/reagent/toxin/polonium.desc: An extremely radioactive material in liquid form. Ingestion results in fatal irradiation.
/datum/reagent/toxin/polonium.name: Polonium

/datum/reagent/toxin/radiomagnetic_disru.desc: A toxic chemical that rapidly destroys nanites and causes highly localized EMPs.
/datum/reagent/toxin/radiomagnetic_disru.name: Radiomagnetic Disruptor

/datum/reagent/toxin/rotatium.desc: A constantly swirling, oddly colourful fluid. Causes the consumer's sense of direction and hand-eye coordination to become wild.
/datum/reagent/toxin/rotatium.name: Rotatium

/datum/reagent/toxin/slimejelly.desc: A gooey semi-liquid produced from one of the deadliest lifeforms in existence. SO REAL.
/datum/reagent/toxin/slimejelly.name: Slime Jelly

/datum/reagent/toxin/sodium_thiopental.desc: Sodium Thiopental induces heavy weakness in its target as well as unconsciousness.
/datum/reagent/toxin/sodium_thiopental.name: Sodium Thiopental

/datum/reagent/toxin/spewium.desc: A powerful emetic, causes uncontrollable vomiting.  May result in vomiting organs at high doses.

/datum/reagent/toxin/spore.desc: A natural toxin produced by blob spores that inhibits vision when ingested.
/datum/reagent/toxin/spore.name: Spore Toxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/spore_burning.desc: A natural toxin produced by blob spores that induces combustion in its victim.
/datum/reagent/toxin/spore_burning.name: Burning Spore Toxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/staminatoxin.desc: A nonlethal poison that causes extreme fatigue and weakness in its victim.
/datum/reagent/toxin/staminatoxin.name: Tirizene

/datum/reagent/toxin/sulfonal.desc: A stealthy poison that deals minor toxin damage and eventually puts the target to sleep.
/datum/reagent/toxin/sulfonal.name: Sulfonal

/datum/reagent/toxin/teapowder.desc: Finely shredded tea leaves, used for making tea.
/datum/reagent/toxin/teapowder.name: Ground Tea Leaves

/datum/reagent/toxin/tetrodotoxin.desc: A colorless, oderless, tasteless neurotoxin usually carried by livers of animals of the Tetraodontiformes order.
/datum/reagent/toxin/tetrodotoxin.name: Tetrodotoxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/venom.desc: An exotic poison extracted from highly toxic fauna. Causes scaling amounts of toxin damage and bruising depending and dosage. Often decays into Histamine.
/datum/reagent/toxin/venom.name: Venom

/datum/reagent/toxin/viperspider.desc: An extremely toxic chemical produced by the rare viper spider. Brings their prey to the brink of death and causes hallucinations.
/datum/reagent/toxin/viperspider.name: Viper Spider Toxin

/datum/reagent/toxin/zombiepowder.desc: A strong neurotoxin that puts the subject into a death-like state.
/datum/reagent/toxin/zombiepowder.name: Zombie Powder

/datum/reagent/universal_indicator.desc: A solution that can be used to create pH paper booklets, or sprayed on things to colour them by their pH.
/datum/reagent/universal_indicator.name: Universal Indicator

/datum/reagent/uranium.desc: A jade-green metallic chemical element in the actinide series, weakly radioactive.
/datum/reagent/uranium.name: Uranium

/datum/reagent/uranium/radium.desc: Radium is an alkaline earth metal. It is extremely radioactive.
/datum/reagent/uranium/radium.name: Radium

/datum/reagent/uranium/uraniumvirusfood.desc: A jade-green metallic chemical element in the actinide series, weakly radioactive.
/datum/reagent/uranium/uraniumvirusfood.name: Decaying Uranium Gel

/datum/reagent/uranium/uraniumvirusfood/.desc: A jade-green metallic chemical element in the actinide series, weakly radioactive.

/datum/reagent/uranium/uraniumvirusfood/.desc: A jade-green metallic chemical element in the actinide series, weakly radioactive.
/datum/reagent/uranium/uraniumvirusfood/.name: Unstable Uranium Gel

/datum/reagent/water.desc: An ubiquitous chemical substance that is composed of hydrogen and oxygen.
/datum/reagent/water.name: Water

/datum/reagent/water/hollowwater.desc: An ubiquitous chemical substance that is composed of hydrogen and oxygen, but it looks kinda hollow.
/datum/reagent/water/hollowwater.name: Hollow Water

/datum/reagent/water/salt.desc: Water, but salty. Smells like... the station infirmary?
